---- MODULE W4Od1m2p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Alpha, Beta, Stations, Runways, NoCtrl, NoRunway

Controllers == Alpha \cup Beta
Sites == {"alpha", "beta"}

SiteOf(c) == IF c \in Alpha THEN "alpha" ELSE "beta"

\* claimed is the per-instance local record; owner is the physical truth.
VARIABLES phase, target, pledge, owner, claimed

vars == << phase, target, pledge, owner, claimed >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in [Controllers -> {"idle", "voting", "holding"}]
    /\ target \in [Controllers -> Runways \cup {NoRunway}]
    /\ pledge \in [Stations -> Controllers \cup {NoCtrl}]
    /\ owner \in [Runways -> Controllers \cup {NoCtrl}]
    /\ claimed \in [Sites -> SUBSET Runways]

Init ==
    /\ phase = [c \in Controllers |-> "idle"]
    /\ target = [c \in Controllers |-> NoRunway]
    /\ pledge = [s \in Stations |-> NoCtrl]
    /\ owner = [r \in Runways |-> NoCtrl]
    /\ claimed = [k \in Sites |-> {}]

Propose(c, r) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "idle"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "voting"]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![c] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED << pledge, owner, claimed >>

\* A station carries at most one outstanding pledge, so a controller holding
\* every pledge has necessarily excluded all of its rivals.
Grant(s, c) ==
    /\ pledge[s] = NoCtrl
    /\ phase[c] = "voting"
    /\ pledge' = [pledge EXCEPT ![s] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED << phase, target, owner, claimed >>

Commit(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "voting"
    /\ \A s \in Stations : pledge[s] = c
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "holding"]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![target[c]] = c]
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![SiteOf(c)] = @ \cup {target[c]}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << target, pledge >>

Abort(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "voting"
    /\ \E s \in Stations : pledge[s] # c /\ pledge[s] # NoCtrl
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![c] = NoRunway]
    /\ pledge' = [s \in Stations |-> IF pledge[s] = c THEN NoCtrl ELSE pledge[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, claimed >>

Release(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = "holding"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![target[c]] = NoCtrl]
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![SiteOf(c)] = @ \ {target[c]}]
    /\ pledge' = [s \in Stations |-> IF pledge[s] = c THEN NoCtrl ELSE pledge[s]]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![c] = NoRunway]

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, r \in Runways : Propose(c, r)
    \/ \E s \in Stations, c \in Controllers : Grant(s, c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Commit(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Abort(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Release(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The two instances never exchange messages: only the shared station
\* pledges keep their local claim records from overlapping.
DisjointInstanceClaims == claimed["alpha"] \cap claimed["beta"] = {}

====
nl:
A regional airport runs runway allocation from two independent allocator instances -- the "alpha" tower complex on the north side and the "beta" complex on the south side. Each instance was commissioned separately and keeps its own local record of which runways it believes it has been granted, but both instances draw from the same physical pool of runways, and both must go through the same shared set of ground-radar stations to obtain a runway.

Each allocator controller is idle, voting, or holding. An idle controller may propose a runway from the shared pool, entering the voting phase with that runway as its target. A radar station that has not yet pledged itself to anyone may grant its vote to a controller that is currently voting; each station holds at most one outstanding pledge. A voting controller that has collected the pledges of every radar station commits: it moves to the holding phase, is recorded as the owner of its target runway, and the runway is added to its own instance's local claim record. A voting controller that observes any station pledged to a different controller aborts: it returns to idle, releases whatever pledges it had collected, and clears its target. A holding controller may release: it returns to idle, the runway's owner record is cleared, the runway is dropped from its instance's claim record, and all of its pledges are returned to the pool of free stations.

The two instances never exchange messages, so nothing but the shared radar stations prevents the north complex and the south complex from both believing they own the same strip of concrete.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The runway sets locally claimed by the alpha instance and by the beta instance are always disjoint, so no runway is ever believed to be owned by both allocator instances at once.

---- MODULE W4Od3m2p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Members, Batches, Capacity, MaxSize, NoBank

\* load is the number of instruction units occupying the settlement window;
\* pledged[b] is the set of member banks that have promised to settle b.
VARIABLES status, size, pledged, load, slow

vars == << status, size, pledged, load, slow >>

Decided == {"committed", "settled", "aborted"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ status \in [Batches -> {"idle", "voting"} \cup Decided]
    /\ size \in [Batches -> 0..MaxSize]
    /\ pledged \in [Batches -> SUBSET Members]
    /\ load \in 0..(Capacity + MaxSize)
    /\ slow \in Members \cup {NoBank}

Init ==
    /\ status = [b \in Batches |-> "idle"]
    /\ size = [b \in Batches |-> 0]
    /\ pledged = [b \in Batches |-> {}]
    /\ load = 0
    /\ slow = NoBank

Elsewhere(m, b) == \E o \in Batches : o # b /\ status[o] = "voting" /\ m \in pledged[o]

Propose(b, n) ==
    /\ status[b] = "idle"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = "voting"]
    /\ size' = [size EXCEPT ![b] = n]
    /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << load, slow >>

\* A bank holds at most one outstanding pledge, so at most one batch can be
\* unanimous at a time and the fit test taken at pledge time stays sound.
Pledge(b, m) ==
    /\ status[b] = "voting"
    /\ m # slow
    /\ m \notin pledged[b]
    /\ ~Elsewhere(m, b)
    /\ load + size[b] <= Capacity
    /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![b] = @ \cup {m}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << status, size, load, slow >>

Commit(b) ==
    /\ status[b] = "voting"
    /\ \A m \in Members : m \in pledged[b]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = "committed"]
    /\ load' = load + size[b]
    /\ UNCHANGED << size, pledged, slow >>

Refuse(b) ==
    /\ status[b] = "voting"
    /\ \/ \E m \in Members : Elsewhere(m, b)
       \/ load + size[b] > Capacity
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = "aborted"]
    /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << size, load, slow >>

Settle(b) ==
    /\ status[b] = "committed"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = "settled"]
    /\ load' = load - size[b]
    /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << size, slow >>

\* At most one member bank is unresponsive at a time, and it is slow rather
\* than failed, so it is always eventually heard from again.
Delay(m) == /\ slow = NoBank /\ slow' = m /\ UNCHANGED << status, size, pledged, load >>
Resume    == /\ slow # NoBank /\ slow' = NoBank /\ UNCHANGED << status, size, pledged, load >>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Batches, n \in 1..MaxSize : Propose(b, n)
    \/ \E b \in Batches, m \in Members : Pledge(b, m)
    \/ \E b \in Batches : Commit(b) \/ Refuse(b) \/ Settle(b)
    \/ (\E m \in Members : Delay(m)) \/ Resume

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Batches : Commit(b))
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Batches : Refuse(b))
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Batches : Settle(b))
    /\ SF_vars(\E b \in Batches, m \in Members : Pledge(b, m))
    /\ WF_vars(Resume)

WindowWithinCapacity == load <= Capacity

EveryVotingBatchDecided ==
    \A b \in Batches : (status[b] = "voting") ~> (status[b] \in Decided)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Members = {bankA, bankB}
    Batches = {bat1, bat2, bat3}
    Capacity = 3
    MaxSize = 2
    NoBank = noBank

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT WindowWithinCapacity

PROPERTY EveryVotingBatchDecided
nl:
A national clearing house settles interbank payments in batches. Each batch is a bundle of payment instructions of some declared size, and the settlement window that the clearing house holds open can carry only a bounded number of instruction units at any one time. Batches are agreed by a two-phase commit across the member banks: a batch is only settled if every member bank has pledged to it.

A batch sits idle until the clearing house proposes it with a declared size, at which point it enters the voting phase with no pledges. A member bank may pledge to a voting batch, but only when that bank is responsive (at most one bank is unresponsive at any moment), only when it has no outstanding pledge to some other voting batch, and only when the batch's declared size still fits in the free part of the settlement window as the bank sees it. A voting batch that has collected pledges from every member bank commits, and its units are added to the window's load. A voting batch that some bank refuses -- because that bank's pledge is already outstanding to another voting batch, or because the batch no longer fits the free window -- is aborted, and its pledges are returned. A committed batch is later settled, at which point its units leave the window. Settled and aborted are final: the clearing house never recycles a batch identifier within a session. Independently, a member bank may become slow and stop answering, and a slow bank may become responsive again; banks here are slow but never failed, so a slow bank always comes back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The settlement window's load never exceeds the clearing house's declared window capacity.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every batch that enters the voting phase is eventually decided, reaching the committed, settled, or aborted state.

---- MODULE W4Od7m0p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS North, South, Moves, MaxVersion, NoMove, NoVersion

Planners == North \cup South

\* snapVer/snapSet are the optimistic snapshot each planner is holding;
\* accepted is the supervisor's handover record of every move ever admitted.
VARIABLES version, plan, snapVer, snapSet, choice, accepted

vars == << version, plan, snapVer, snapSet, choice, accepted >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
    /\ plan \in SUBSET Moves
    /\ snapVer \in [Planners -> (0..MaxVersion) \cup {NoVersion}]
    /\ snapSet \in [Planners -> SUBSET Moves]
    /\ choice \in [Planners -> Moves \cup {NoMove}]
    /\ accepted \in SUBSET Moves

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ plan = {}
    /\ snapVer = [p \in Planners |-> NoVersion]
    /\ snapSet = [p \in Planners |-> {}]
    /\ choice = [p \in Planners |-> NoMove]
    /\ accepted = {}

ReadPlan(p) ==
    /\ snapVer[p] = NoVersion
    /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![p] = version]
    /\ snapSet' = [snapSet EXCEPT ![p] = plan]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, plan, choice, accepted >>

Choose(p, mv) ==
    /\ snapVer[p] # NoVersion
    /\ choice[p] = NoMove
    /\ choice' = [choice EXCEPT ![p] = mv]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, plan, snapVer, snapSet, accepted >>

\* The version test is the whole of the concurrency control: a planner writes
\* its own snapshot back, so a commit on a stale stamp would erase the moves
\* that landed in between.
Commit(p) ==
    /\ snapVer[p] = version
    /\ choice[p] # NoMove
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ plan' = snapSet[p] \cup {choice[p]}
    /\ accepted' = accepted \cup {choice[p]}
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![p] = NoVersion]
    /\ snapSet' = [snapSet EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
    /\ choice' = [choice EXCEPT ![p] = NoMove]

Retry(p) ==
    /\ snapVer[p] # NoVersion
    /\ snapVer[p] # version
    /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![p] = NoVersion]
    /\ snapSet' = [snapSet EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
    /\ choice' = [choice EXCEPT ![p] = NoMove]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, plan, accepted >>

DropChoice(p) ==
    /\ choice[p] # NoMove
    /\ choice' = [choice EXCEPT ![p] = NoMove]
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, plan, snapVer, snapSet, accepted >>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Planners : ReadPlan(p) \/ Commit(p) \/ Retry(p) \/ DropChoice(p)
    \/ \E p \in Planners, mv \in Moves : Choose(p, mv)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No accepted move is ever lost from the plan, whichever office committed it.
NoLostCraneMove == accepted \subseteq plan

====
nl:
A container terminal keeps a single stowage plan for the crane yard: a record listing which crane moves have been accepted for the current shift. The terminal is operated by two independently commissioned yard-management instances, the north gantry office and the south gantry office, whose planners share that one plan record. Because neither office will wait on the other, updates are applied optimistically: a planner reads the plan, decides on a move, and writes back only if the plan has not changed underneath it.

A planner with no snapshot in hand reads the record, taking both its version stamp and a copy of its accepted-move set. A planner holding a snapshot but no chosen move picks a crane move from the shared move pool. A planner holding a snapshot and a chosen move commits if the record's version stamp still matches the stamp it read: the record's accepted-move set becomes the planner's snapshot plus its chosen move, the version stamp advances, and the planner's snapshot and choice are cleared. A planner whose snapshot version no longer matches the record retries: it discards its snapshot and its chosen move and will read again. A planner may also simply drop its chosen move while keeping its snapshot, so it can choose differently.

The yard supervisor separately records every move that has ever been accepted into the plan, which is how a dropped move would be noticed at shift handover.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every crane move that has ever been accepted into the stowage plan is still present in the plan's accepted-move set, so no office's commit ever silently discards another office's move.

---- MODULE W4Od6m9p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Calls, MaxEpoch, NoCar, NoCall

\* carEpoch[c] is the configuration epoch car c last registered under; the
\* controller only recognises cars whose epoch equals its own.
VARIABLES epoch, carEpoch, held, waiting, done, mute

vars == << epoch, carEpoch, held, waiting, done, mute >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ carEpoch \in [Cars -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ held \in [Cars -> Calls \cup {NoCall}]
    /\ waiting \in SUBSET Calls
    /\ done \in SUBSET Calls
    /\ mute \in Cars \cup {NoCar}

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ carEpoch = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ held = [c \in Cars |-> NoCall]
    /\ waiting = {}
    /\ done = {}
    /\ mute = NoCar

Assigned(k) == \E c \in Cars : held[c] = k

Raise(k) ==
    /\ k \notin waiting /\ k \notin done /\ ~Assigned(k)
    /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {k}
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, carEpoch, held, done, mute >>

Take(c, k) ==
    /\ carEpoch[c] = epoch
    /\ c # mute
    /\ held[c] = NoCall
    /\ k \in waiting
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![c] = k]
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {k}
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, carEpoch, done, mute >>

Serve(c) ==
    /\ held[c] # NoCall
    /\ carEpoch[c] = epoch
    /\ done' = done \cup {held[c]}
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![c] = NoCall]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, carEpoch, waiting, mute >>

\* Reconfiguration invalidates every car at once, so in-flight assignments
\* must go back to the waiting set rather than ride out the epoch change.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {k \in Calls : Assigned(k)}
    /\ held' = [c \in Cars |-> NoCall]
    /\ UNCHANGED << carEpoch, done, mute >>

Register(c) ==
    /\ carEpoch[c] # epoch
    /\ c # mute
    /\ carEpoch' = [carEpoch EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, held, waiting, done, mute >>

GoMute(c) == /\ mute = NoCar /\ mute' = c /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, carEpoch, held, waiting, done >>
Answer    == /\ mute # NoCar /\ mute' = NoCar /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, carEpoch, held, waiting, done >>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Calls : Raise(k)
    \/ \E c \in Cars, k \in Calls : Take(c, k)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Serve(c) \/ Register(c) \/ GoMute(c)
    \/ Reconfigure \/ Answer

\* A car that is not answering blocks taking and re-registering only
\* intermittently, so those need strong fairness; the schedule has finitely
\* many epochs and each call is raised once, so each fair action below can
\* still fire only finitely often.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ SF_vars(\E c \in Cars, k \in Calls : Take(c, k))
    /\ SF_vars(\E c \in Cars : Serve(c))
    /\ SF_vars(\E c \in Cars : Register(c))
    /\ WF_vars(Answer)

NoStaleCarHoldsCall ==
    \A c \in Cars : held[c] # NoCall => carEpoch[c] = epoch

EveryCallCompleted ==
    \A k \in Calls : (k \in waiting) ~> (k \in done)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {carA, carB}
    Calls = {flr3, flr7}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NoCar = noCar
    NoCall = noCall

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoStaleCarHoldsCall

PROPERTY EveryCallCompleted
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank is driven by a group controller that periodically reconfigures itself -- when a car is taken out for maintenance or a new dispatch profile is loaded, the controller advances its configuration epoch. Every car carries the epoch it last registered under, and the controller will only let a car act on the bank's behalf while that car's epoch matches the controller's current one. Cars are slow rather than failed: a car may stop responding for a while, but it always answers eventually.

A hall call at a floor may be raised if it is not already waiting, assigned, or completed. A car whose registered epoch matches the controller's and that is currently free may take a waiting hall call, which removes the call from the waiting set. A car holding a call whose registered epoch still matches the controller's may serve the call, completing it and freeing the car. The controller may reconfigure while it has epochs left in its commissioning schedule: the epoch advances, and every in-flight assignment is dropped back into the waiting set, because no car is registered under the new epoch yet. A car whose registered epoch is behind the controller's may re-register, adopting the current epoch. A car may also become the one unresponsive car in the bank, and the unresponsive car may start answering again; a car that is not answering neither takes calls nor re-registers.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A car never holds an assigned hall call unless the epoch it registered under is the group controller's current epoch, so no stale car ever acts on the bank's behalf.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every hall call that is raised is eventually completed.

---- MODULE W4Od18m8p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Phones, Zones, Fittings, MaxBudget, NoPhone, NoLock

\* A lock is addressed coarse-then-fine: the zone first, then the fitting.
Locks == Zones \X Fittings
ZoneOf(l) == l[1]

VARIABLES zoneGrant, session, budget, want, booked

vars == << zoneGrant, session, budget, want, booked >>

OpenCount == Cardinality({l \in Locks : session[l] # NoPhone})
Committed == OpenCount + Cardinality(booked)

TypeOK ==
    /\ zoneGrant \in [Zones -> Phones \cup {NoPhone}]
    /\ session \in [Locks -> Phones \cup {NoPhone}]
    /\ budget \in 0..MaxBudget
    /\ want \in [Phones -> Locks \cup {NoLock}]
    /\ booked \in SUBSET Phones

Init ==
    /\ zoneGrant = [z \in Zones |-> NoPhone]
    /\ session = [l \in Locks |-> NoPhone]
    /\ budget = 1
    /\ want = [p \in Phones |-> NoLock]
    /\ booked = {}

Request(p, l) ==
    /\ want[p] = NoLock
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![p] = l]
    /\ UNCHANGED << zoneGrant, session, budget, booked >>

\* The capacity reservation is booked with the coarse grant, before the fine
\* grant exists, so a phone in the middle of the hierarchy still occupies the
\* budget it is going to spend.
TakeZone(p) ==
    /\ want[p] # NoLock
    /\ p \notin booked
    /\ zoneGrant[ZoneOf(want[p])] = NoPhone
    /\ Committed < budget
    /\ zoneGrant' = [zoneGrant EXCEPT ![ZoneOf(want[p])] = p]
    /\ booked' = booked \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED << session, budget, want >>

OpenSession(p) ==
    /\ p \in booked
    /\ want[p] # NoLock
    /\ zoneGrant[ZoneOf(want[p])] = p
    /\ session[want[p]] = NoPhone
    /\ session' = [session EXCEPT ![want[p]] = p]
    /\ booked' = booked \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED << zoneGrant, budget, want >>

GiveUp(p) ==
    /\ p \in booked
    /\ zoneGrant' = [z \in Zones |-> IF zoneGrant[z] = p THEN NoPhone ELSE zoneGrant[z]]
    /\ booked' = booked \ {p}
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![p] = NoLock]
    /\ UNCHANGED << session, budget >>

Close(p) ==
    /\ p \notin booked
    /\ want[p] # NoLock
    /\ session' = [l \in Locks |-> IF session[l] = p THEN NoPhone ELSE session[l]]
    /\ zoneGrant' = [z \in Zones |-> IF zoneGrant[z] = p THEN NoPhone ELSE zoneGrant[z]]
    /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![p] = NoLock]
    /\ UNCHANGED << budget, booked >>

\* The installer may raise or lower the radio budget, but never below what the
\* hub has already committed.
Reprovision(n) ==
    /\ n >= Committed
    /\ budget' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED << zoneGrant, session, want, booked >>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Phones, l \in Locks : Request(p, l)
    \/ \E p \in Phones : TakeZone(p) \/ OpenSession(p) \/ GiveUp(p) \/ Close(p)
    \/ \E n \in 0..MaxBudget : Reprovision(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BudgetNeverOversubscribed == Committed <= budget

====
nl:
A smart-home hub mediates unlock sessions for the door locks in a house. Locks are addressed hierarchically: every lock belongs to a zone, and a phone that wants to open a lock must first take the zone's coarse grant and only then the lock's own fine grant. The hub's radio can sustain only a bounded number of concurrent unlock sessions, and that budget is not fixed: the installer re-provisions it at runtime as the mesh grows or as interference forces the hub to back off.

A phone with nothing in progress may request a particular lock. A phone holding a request may take the coarse grant for that lock's zone, provided the zone is not already granted to another phone, the phone does not already hold a capacity reservation, and the sessions currently open plus the reservations currently outstanding are strictly below the hub's budget -- taking the zone grant also books the phone's capacity reservation. A phone that holds a reservation and the coarse grant covering its requested lock may open the session on that lock, which consumes its reservation. A phone may close: the session on its lock, its zone grant, its reservation, and its request are all released. A phone that has taken a zone grant but not yet opened a session may give up instead, releasing the zone grant and the reservation without opening anything. The installer may re-provision the hub's budget to any value that is not below the sessions currently open plus the reservations currently outstanding.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of unlock sessions currently open plus the number of outstanding capacity reservations never exceeds the hub's currently provisioned budget.

---- MODULE W4Od10m9p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks, MaxEpoch, Running

Home == CHOOSE b \in Blocks : TRUE

\* pos is where the trains physically are; berthed/running are the signalling
\* controller's manifest, which is what the safety property is about.
VARIABLES pos, berthed, running, epoch, blockEpoch, dead

vars == << pos, berthed, running, epoch, blockEpoch, dead >>

RECURSIVE Tally(_)
Tally(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN berthed[b] + Tally(S \ {b})

Fleet == Cardinality(Trains)

TypeOK ==
    /\ pos \in [Trains -> Blocks \cup {Running}]
    /\ berthed \in [Blocks -> 0..Fleet]
    /\ running \in 0..Fleet
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ blockEpoch \in [Blocks -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ dead \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ pos = [t \in Trains |-> Home]
    /\ berthed = [b \in Blocks |-> IF b = Home THEN Fleet ELSE 0]
    /\ running = 0
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ blockEpoch = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ dead = FALSE

Depart(t) ==
    /\ pos[t] \in Blocks
    /\ berthed' = [berthed EXCEPT ![pos[t]] = @ - 1]
    /\ running' = running + 1
    /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![t] = Running]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, blockEpoch, dead >>

\* A block only takes a train once it carries the epoch the controller last
\* broadcast; the manifest moves the train in the same step it physically does.
Arrive(t, b) ==
    /\ pos[t] = Running
    /\ blockEpoch[b] = epoch
    /\ berthed' = [berthed EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ running' = running - 1
    /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![t] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, blockEpoch, dead >>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ ~dead
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << pos, berthed, running, blockEpoch, dead >>

Resync(b) ==
    /\ blockEpoch[b] # epoch
    /\ blockEpoch' = [blockEpoch EXCEPT ![b] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED << pos, berthed, running, epoch, dead >>

\* A silent crash: no announcement, the epoch simply stops moving.
Crash ==
    /\ ~dead
    /\ dead' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED << pos, berthed, running, epoch, blockEpoch >>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Depart(t)
    \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Arrive(t, b)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : Resync(b)
    \/ Reconfigure \/ Crash

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A t \in Trains :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ SF_vars(\E b \in Blocks : Arrive(t, b))
    /\ \A b \in Blocks :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(Resync(b))

ManifestConservesTrains == Tally(Blocks) + running = Fleet

EveryRunningTrainBerths ==
    \A t \in Trains : (pos[t] = Running) ~> (pos[t] \in Blocks)

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Trains = {trn1, trn2}
    Blocks = {blkA, blkB}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    Running = running

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ManifestConservesTrains

PROPERTY EveryRunningTrainBerths
nl:
A subway line is divided into signalling blocks. Every train is either berthed in exactly one block or running between blocks, and the line's signalling controller keeps a manifest: a per-block count of berthed trains plus a count of trains currently running. The controller is periodically reconfigured -- a track possession, a timetable change -- and each reconfiguration advances its signalling epoch. A block will only accept an arriving train once it has resynchronised to the controller's current epoch. The controller itself can crash silently: it simply stops reconfiguring, and nobody is told, but the epoch it last broadcast is still latched in the trackside equipment, so blocks can still resynchronise to it.

A berthed train may depart: it leaves its block, the manifest count for that block is decremented, and the running count is incremented. A train that is running may arrive into any block that has resynchronised to the current epoch: the manifest count for that block is incremented and the running count is decremented. The controller may reconfigure while it is alive and has possessions left in its schedule, advancing the epoch. A block whose latched epoch is behind the controller's may resynchronise to it. The controller may crash, after which it never reconfigures again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The manifest's per-block berthed counts plus its running count always sum to exactly the number of trains on the line, so the signalling manifest never creates or loses a train.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every train that is running between blocks eventually berths in some block.

---- MODULE W4Od9m9p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Relays, MaxEpoch, NoRelay

\* authorised is the dispatcher's list for the CURRENT epoch only; relayEpoch
\* records how far behind the scheme each relay has fallen.
VARIABLES epoch, relayEpoch, authorised, shedding, offline

vars == << epoch, relayEpoch, authorised, shedding, offline >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ relayEpoch \in [Relays -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ authorised \in SUBSET Relays
    /\ shedding \in SUBSET Relays
    /\ offline \in Relays \cup {NoRelay}

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ relayEpoch = [r \in Relays |-> 0]
    /\ authorised = {}
    /\ shedding = {}
    /\ offline = NoRelay

Authorise(r) ==
    /\ r \notin authorised
    /\ authorised' = authorised \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, relayEpoch, shedding, offline >>

\* Withdrawal reaches the relay in the same telemetry cycle, so it can only be
\* issued to a relay that is actually in contact.
Withdraw(r) ==
    /\ r \in authorised
    /\ r # offline
    /\ authorised' = authorised \ {r}
    /\ shedding' = shedding \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, relayEpoch, offline >>

Shed(r) ==
    /\ r # offline
    /\ relayEpoch[r] = epoch
    /\ r \in authorised
    /\ r \notin shedding
    /\ shedding' = shedding \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, relayEpoch, authorised, offline >>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ authorised' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED << relayEpoch, shedding, offline >>

\* Catching up is also when a relay learns its authorisation was voided, so
\* resynchronising has to restore load the relay is no longer entitled to shed.
Resync(r) ==
    /\ r # offline
    /\ relayEpoch[r] # epoch
    /\ relayEpoch' = [relayEpoch EXCEPT ![r] = epoch]
    /\ shedding' = IF r \in authorised THEN shedding ELSE shedding \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, authorised, offline >>

DropOut(r) == /\ offline = NoRelay /\ offline' = r /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, relayEpoch, authorised, shedding >>
Return     == /\ offline # NoRelay /\ offline' = NoRelay /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, relayEpoch, authorised, shedding >>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Relays : Authorise(r) \/ Withdraw(r) \/ Shed(r) \/ Resync(r) \/ DropOut(r)
    \/ Reconfigure \/ Return

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SyncedRelaysShedOnlyIfAuthorised ==
    \A r \in Relays : (r \in shedding /\ relayEpoch[r] = epoch) => r \in authorised

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Relays = {fdr1, fdr2, fdr3}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NoRelay = noRelay

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SyncedRelaysShedOnlyIfAuthorised
nl:
A regional power grid runs an automatic load-shedding scheme. A dispatcher maintains, for the current scheme configuration, the list of feeder relays it authorises to shed load. The scheme is reconfigured whenever the network topology changes -- a line is switched out, a generator is redispatched -- and each reconfiguration advances the scheme's epoch and voids every authorisation issued under the previous one. Each relay carries the epoch it last synchronised to. Relays are slow rather than failed: at most one relay at a time is out of contact, and it always comes back.

The dispatcher may authorise a relay, adding it to the current authorisation list. The dispatcher may withdraw a relay's authorisation, but only while that relay is in contact, and withdrawing also commands the relay to restore whatever load it is shedding. A relay that is in contact, is synchronised to the current epoch, and is on the authorisation list may begin shedding load. The dispatcher may reconfigure the scheme while it has reconfigurations left in its schedule: the epoch advances and the authorisation list is emptied. A relay that is in contact and whose synchronised epoch is behind the scheme's may resynchronise; on resynchronising it adopts the current epoch and, if it is not on the current authorisation list, it restores the load it was shedding. Finally, the one relay in contact may drop out of contact, and a relay out of contact may return.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A relay that has synchronised to the scheme's current epoch is never shedding load unless the dispatcher's current authorisation list contains it.

---- MODULE W4Od3m9p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Instructions, MaxEpoch, MaxCapacity, NoStamp

\* record is the shared settlement record; accepted is the clearing house's
\* audit trail of every instruction ever posted into it.
VARIABLES epoch, record, accepted, copy, stamp, capacity

vars == << epoch, record, accepted, copy, stamp, capacity >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ record \in SUBSET Instructions
    /\ accepted \in SUBSET Instructions
    /\ copy \in [Nodes -> SUBSET Instructions]
    /\ stamp \in [Nodes -> (0..MaxEpoch) \cup {NoStamp}]
    /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCapacity

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ record = {}
    /\ accepted = {}
    /\ copy = [n \in Nodes |-> {}]
    /\ stamp = [n \in Nodes |-> NoStamp]
    /\ capacity = 1

ReRead(n) ==
    /\ stamp[n] # epoch
    /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![n] = record]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![n] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, record, accepted, capacity >>

\* Posting advances the epoch, so every working copy in the service -- the
\* writer's included -- is stale the instant the record changes.
Post(n, x) ==
    /\ stamp[n] = epoch
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ x \notin accepted
    /\ Cardinality(copy[n] \cup {x}) <= capacity
    /\ record' = copy[n] \cup {x}
    /\ accepted' = accepted \cup {x}
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << copy, stamp, capacity >>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << record, accepted, copy, stamp, capacity >>

\* Capacity moves at runtime but never below what is already carried.
Reprovision(c) ==
    /\ c # capacity
    /\ c >= Cardinality(record)
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, record, accepted, copy, stamp >>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : ReRead(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, x \in Instructions : Post(n, x)
    \/ \E c \in 0..MaxCapacity : Reprovision(c)
    \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A n \in Nodes :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(ReRead(n))

CurrentCopiesCarryEveryAcceptedInstruction ==
    \A n \in Nodes : stamp[n] = epoch => accepted \subseteq copy[n]

EveryStaleCopyRefreshes ==
    \A n \in Nodes : (stamp[n] # epoch) ~> (stamp[n] = epoch)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {setA, setB}
    Instructions = {pay1, pay2}
    MaxEpoch = 3
    MaxCapacity = 3
    NoStamp = noStamp

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CurrentCopiesCarryEveryAcceptedInstruction

PROPERTY EveryStaleCopyRefreshes
nl:
A clearing house keeps one shared settlement record: the set of payment instructions accepted for the current session. Several settlement nodes maintain that record, and the service runs in numbered configurations -- every time the record is written, or the operations desk reconfigures the service, the configuration epoch advances. A node works from a private working copy stamped with the epoch it read, and a node may only write the record back while its stamp is still the service's current epoch. The desk also re-provisions the session's carrying capacity at runtime, raising or lowering the number of instructions the record may hold, though never below what the record already holds.

A node whose working copy is stamped with something other than the current epoch re-reads: it copies the record and takes the current epoch as its stamp. A node whose stamp is current may post an instruction that is not yet accepted, provided the record it would write -- its working copy plus that instruction -- still fits the session's capacity; posting replaces the shared record with that set, marks the instruction accepted in the clearing house's audit trail, and advances the epoch, which by construction leaves every node's working copy stale, including its own. The operations desk may reconfigure the service without posting anything, which also advances the epoch. The desk may re-provision the capacity to any different value that is at least the size of the current record.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any settlement node whose working copy is stamped with the service's current epoch holds every instruction the audit trail has ever accepted, so no node can write the record back in a form that drops an accepted instruction.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every settlement node whose working copy has gone stale eventually holds a working copy stamped with the current epoch again.

---- MODULE W4Od8m6p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, Courses, Cap, LeaseTicks, MaxOverrides, NoCourse

\* A live hold occupies a seat just as a confirmed enrolment does, so both
\* sides of the sum below have to be counted against the cap.
VARIABLES enrolled, hold, ttl, overrides

vars == << enrolled, hold, ttl, overrides >>

Occupancy(c) ==
    Cardinality(enrolled[c]) + Cardinality({s \in Students : hold[s] = c})

TypeOK ==
    /\ enrolled \in [Courses -> SUBSET Students]
    /\ hold \in [Students -> Courses \cup {NoCourse}]
    /\ ttl \in [Students -> 0..LeaseTicks]
    /\ overrides \in 0..MaxOverrides

Init ==
    /\ enrolled = [c \in Courses |-> {}]
    /\ hold = [s \in Students |-> NoCourse]
    /\ ttl = [s \in Students |-> 0]
    /\ overrides = 0

TakeHold(s, c) ==
    /\ hold[s] = NoCourse
    /\ s \notin enrolled[c]
    /\ Occupancy(c) < Cap
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![s] = c]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = LeaseTicks]
    /\ UNCHANGED << enrolled, overrides >>

Confirm(s) ==
    /\ hold[s] # NoCourse
    /\ ttl[s] > 0
    /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![hold[s]] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![s] = NoCourse]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED << overrides >>

\* The clock runs down every live lease at once.
Tick ==
    /\ \E s \in Students : hold[s] # NoCourse /\ ttl[s] > 0
    /\ ttl' = [s \in Students |->
                 IF hold[s] # NoCourse /\ ttl[s] > 0 THEN ttl[s] - 1 ELSE ttl[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << enrolled, hold, overrides >>

Lapse(s) ==
    /\ hold[s] # NoCourse
    /\ ttl[s] = 0
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![s] = NoCourse]
    /\ UNCHANGED << enrolled, ttl, overrides >>

Revoke(s) ==
    /\ hold[s] # NoCourse
    /\ overrides < MaxOverrides
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![s] = NoCourse]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
    /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << enrolled >>

\* The registrar's override skips the lease but not the seat cap.
ForceEnrol(s, c) ==
    /\ hold[s] = NoCourse
    /\ s \notin enrolled[c]
    /\ overrides < MaxOverrides
    /\ Occupancy(c) < Cap
    /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![c] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << hold, ttl >>

Drop(s, c) ==
    /\ s \in enrolled[c]
    /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![c] = @ \ {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << hold, ttl, overrides >>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Students, c \in Courses : TakeHold(s, c) \/ ForceEnrol(s, c) \/ Drop(s, c)
    \/ \E s \in Students : Confirm(s) \/ Lapse(s) \/ Revoke(s)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SeatCapNeverOversold == \A c \in Courses : Occupancy(c) <= Cap

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Students = {stu1, stu2}
    Courses = {crs1, crs2}
    Cap = 1
    LeaseTicks = 2
    MaxOverrides = 2
    NoCourse = noCourse

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SeatCapNeverOversold
nl:
A university runs course registration on a hold-and-confirm scheme. Each course has a fixed seat cap. A student who wants a course first takes a hold on a seat; the hold is a lease that carries a countdown and lapses if the student does not confirm in time. A seat that is under an unexpired hold counts against the cap exactly as a confirmed enrolment does, because the registrar will not oversell a room. The registrar's office additionally has a bounded number of privileged overrides it may spend during a registration period.

A student with no hold outstanding may take a hold on a course they are not already enrolled in, provided the course's confirmed enrolments plus its outstanding holds are strictly below its cap; the hold starts with a full lease countdown. A student holding a lease that has not run down may confirm, which turns the hold into a confirmed enrolment. The registration clock may tick while at least one live lease is outstanding, running down the countdown on every outstanding hold. A student whose lease has run to zero loses the hold. The registrar may revoke any outstanding hold immediately, spending one override. The registrar may also directly enrol a student who has no hold outstanding into a course they are not in, again spending one override, and again only while that course's enrolments plus holds are strictly below its cap. A confirmed student may drop the course.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every course, its confirmed enrolments plus its outstanding seat holds never exceed that course's seat cap.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m5p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS RidgeWing, ValleyWing, Stations, Heavy, Budget, Loiter, NoDrone

Drones == RidgeWing \cup ValleyWing

\* Both wings bill against one budget; a heavy airframe costs two shares.
Cost(d) == IF d \in Heavy THEN 2 ELSE 1

\* fuel is the loiter time left to an airborne drone; it must land at zero.
VARIABLES phase, vote, airspace, fuel

vars == << phase, vote, airspace, fuel >>

RECURSIVE Burn(_)
Burn(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET d == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN
         (IF phase[d] = "airborne" THEN Cost(d) ELSE 0) + Burn(S \ {d})

Consumed == Burn(Drones)
Majority(d) == 2 * Cardinality({s \in Stations : vote[s] = d}) > Cardinality(Stations)

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in [Drones -> {"grounded", "seeking", "airborne", "refused"}]
    /\ vote \in [Stations -> Drones \cup {NoDrone}]
    /\ airspace \in {"open", "closed"}
    /\ fuel \in [Drones -> 0..Loiter]

Init ==
    /\ phase = [d \in Drones |-> "grounded"]
    /\ vote = [s \in Stations |-> NoDrone]
    /\ airspace = "open"
    /\ fuel = [d \in Drones |-> 0]

Release(d) == [s \in Stations |-> IF vote[s] = d THEN NoDrone ELSE vote[s]]

Request(d) ==
    /\ phase[d] = "grounded"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "seeking"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << vote, airspace, fuel >>

\* A station carries one vote, so two seekers can never both hold a majority.
CastVote(s, d) ==
    /\ vote[s] = NoDrone
    /\ phase[d] = "seeking"
    /\ airspace = "open"
    /\ Consumed + Cost(d) <= Budget
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![s] = d]
    /\ UNCHANGED << phase, airspace, fuel >>

Launch(d) ==
    /\ phase[d] = "seeking"
    /\ Majority(d)
    /\ airspace = "open"
    /\ Consumed + Cost(d) <= Budget
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "airborne"]
    /\ vote' = Release(d)
    /\ fuel' = [fuel EXCEPT ![d] = Loiter]
    /\ UNCHANGED << airspace >>

Refuse(d) ==
    /\ phase[d] = "seeking"
    /\ \/ airspace = "closed"
       \/ Consumed + Cost(d) > Budget
       \/ \E s \in Stations : vote[s] # NoDrone /\ vote[s] # d
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "refused"]
    /\ vote' = Release(d)
    /\ UNCHANGED << airspace, fuel >>

\* A drone is only released from the budget once it is actually down, and it
\* cannot come down before its loiter time has run out.
Land(d) ==
    /\ phase[d] = "airborne"
    /\ fuel[d] = 0
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "grounded"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << vote, airspace, fuel >>

BurnFuel ==
    /\ \E d \in Drones : phase[d] = "airborne" /\ fuel[d] > 0
    /\ fuel' = [d \in Drones |->
                  IF phase[d] = "airborne" /\ fuel[d] > 0 THEN fuel[d] - 1 ELSE fuel[d]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << phase, vote, airspace >>

Reset(d) ==
    /\ phase[d] = "refused"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "grounded"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << vote, airspace, fuel >>

CloseAirspace == /\ airspace = "open" /\ airspace' = "closed" /\ UNCHANGED << phase, vote, fuel >>
OpenAirspace  == /\ airspace = "closed" /\ airspace' = "open" /\ UNCHANGED << phase, vote, fuel >>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Request(d) \/ Launch(d) \/ Refuse(d) \/ Land(d) \/ Reset(d)
    \/ \E s \in Stations, d \in Drones : CastVote(s, d)
    \/ CloseAirspace \/ OpenAirspace \/ BurnFuel

\* Both decisions flicker with the airspace and with the budget, so each
\* seeker needs strong fairness on its own launch and its own refusal.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A d \in Drones :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ SF_vars(\E s \in Stations : CastVote(s, d))
        /\ SF_vars(Launch(d))
        /\ SF_vars(Refuse(d))

EnduranceBudgetRespected == Consumed <= Budget

EverySeekerDecided ==
    \A d \in Drones : (phase[d] = "seeking") ~> (phase[d] \in {"airborne", "refused"})

====
nl:
A wildfire surveillance operation flies two separately commissioned drone wings -- the ridge wing and the valley wing -- over the same fire. The two wings were procured independently and do not coordinate with each other, but they draw on one shared resource: the incident's airspace endurance budget. Every airborne drone consumes a share of that budget according to its payload class, heavy drones consuming more than light ones, and the incident commander will not let the total consumption of the airborne fleet exceed the budget. A drone may only launch after winning a majority of the ground stations' votes; each station holds at most one outstanding vote.

A grounded drone may request launch, entering the seeking state with no votes. A ground station with no outstanding vote may vote for a seeking drone, provided the airspace is open and the budget still has room for that drone's payload class as the station sees it. A seeking drone holding a majority of the stations' votes may launch when the airspace is open and its payload still fits the remaining budget; launching releases its votes. A seeking drone is refused when the airspace is closed, when its payload no longer fits the remaining budget, or when some station's vote is outstanding to a different seeking drone; being refused also releases its votes. An airborne drone burns loiter time while it flies, and the whole airborne fleet burns a tick together; a drone whose loiter time has run out lands, returning its share of the budget. A refused drone may be reset to grounded and may try again. The incident commander may close the airspace and may reopen it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total endurance consumed by the airborne drones of both wings together never exceeds the incident's endurance budget.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every drone that enters the seeking state is eventually either launched or refused.

---- MODULE W4Od17m2p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bags, Sectors, Chutes, ChuteLimit, NoChute, NoSector

VARIABLES status, chute, pledged, crashed

vars == << status, chute, pledged, crashed >>

\* A bag that is still voting has already booked its place in the chute, so
\* both the travelling and the delivered bags count against the limit.
Occupancy(ch) ==
    Cardinality({b \in Bags : chute[b] = ch /\ status[b] \in {"voting", "delivered"}})

TypeOK ==
    /\ status \in [Bags -> {"queued", "voting", "delivered", "cleared", "rejected"}]
    /\ chute \in [Bags -> Chutes \cup {NoChute}]
    /\ pledged \in [Bags -> SUBSET Sectors]
    /\ crashed \in Sectors \cup {NoSector}

Init ==
    /\ status = [b \in Bags |-> "queued"]
    /\ chute = [b \in Bags |-> NoChute]
    /\ pledged = [b \in Bags |-> {}]
    /\ crashed = NoSector

Propose(b, ch) ==
    /\ status[b] = "queued"
    /\ Occupancy(ch) < ChuteLimit
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = "voting"]
    /\ chute' = [chute EXCEPT ![b] = ch]
    /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << crashed >>

Pledge(s, b) ==
    /\ status[b] = "voting"
    /\ s # crashed
    /\ s \notin pledged[b]
    /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![b] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << status, chute, crashed >>

Commit(b) ==
    /\ status[b] = "voting"
    /\ \A s \in Sectors : s \in pledged[b]
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = "delivered"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << chute, pledged, crashed >>

\* Timing out is the router's only remedy against a controller that has gone
\* quiet without saying so; it also gives the chute place back.
TimeOut(b) ==
    /\ status[b] = "voting"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = "rejected"]
    /\ chute' = [chute EXCEPT ![b] = NoChute]
    /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << crashed >>

Clear(b) ==
    /\ status[b] = "delivered"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = "cleared"]
    /\ chute' = [chute EXCEPT ![b] = NoChute]
    /\ UNCHANGED << pledged, crashed >>

Requeue(b) ==
    /\ status[b] \in {"cleared", "rejected"}
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![b] = "queued"]
    /\ pledged' = [pledged EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << chute, crashed >>

Crash(s) ==
    /\ crashed = NoSector
    /\ crashed' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED << status, chute, pledged >>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Bags, ch \in Chutes : Propose(b, ch)
    \/ \E s \in Sectors, b \in Bags : Pledge(s, b)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : Commit(b) \/ TimeOut(b) \/ Clear(b) \/ Requeue(b)
    \/ \E s \in Sectors : Crash(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ChuteNeverOverfilled == \A ch \in Chutes : Occupancy(ch) <= ChuteLimit

====
nl:
An airport baggage router decides, for each bag, which make-up chute it will be sent to. A chute holds only so many bags before the handlers must clear it, so the router will not commit a bag to a chute that is already at its limit -- and a bag that has been committed to a chute but is still travelling counts against that chute just as a bag already sitting in it does. Each routing decision is agreed by a two-phase commit across the sector controllers that own the belts along the way. One sector controller may crash silently: it stops answering, and the router is never told, so the router can only recover by timing the bag out.

A queued bag may be proposed to a chute, provided that chute's bags already delivered plus the bags already travelling to it are below its limit; the bag then enters the voting phase with no sector pledges. A sector controller that has not crashed may pledge to a voting bag it has not yet pledged to. A voting bag that has collected pledges from every sector controller is committed and travels to its chute. The router may time out a voting bag at any point, rejecting it and returning its pledges, which is the only way a bag stuck behind a crashed controller is ever cleared. A bag that has arrived at its chute is later cleared by the handlers, freeing its place. A cleared or rejected bag may be re-queued for another attempt. At most one sector controller ever crashes, and it does so silently.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every make-up chute, the bags already delivered to it plus the bags committed and still travelling to it never exceed that chute's limit.

---- MODULE W4Od16m8p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Techs, Cabinets, Slots, MaxArms, NoTech

\* A bin is addressed coarse-then-fine: cabinet first, then slot within it.
Bins == Cabinets \X Slots
CabinetOf(b) == b[1]

VARIABLES coarse, fine, allowance, permits

vars == << coarse, fine, allowance, permits >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in [Cabinets -> Techs \cup {NoTech}]
    /\ fine \in [Bins -> Techs \cup {NoTech}]
    /\ allowance \in 0..MaxArms
    /\ permits \in SUBSET Techs

Init ==
    /\ coarse = [c \in Cabinets |-> NoTech]
    /\ fine = [b \in Bins |-> NoTech]
    /\ allowance = 1
    /\ permits = {}

TakePermit(t) ==
    /\ t \notin permits
    /\ Cardinality(permits) < allowance
    /\ permits' = permits \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, fine, allowance >>

TakeCabinet(t, c) ==
    /\ t \in permits
    /\ coarse[c] = NoTech
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![c] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED << fine, allowance, permits >>

TakeBin(t, b) ==
    /\ coarse[CabinetOf(b)] = t
    /\ fine[b] = NoTech
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, allowance, permits >>

ReleaseBin(t, b) ==
    /\ fine[b] = t
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = NoTech]
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, allowance, permits >>

\* Interlocks are surrendered fine before coarse: a cabinet cannot be given up
\* while the technician still holds a bin inside it.
ReleaseCabinet(t, c) ==
    /\ coarse[c] = t
    /\ \A b \in Bins : CabinetOf(b) = c => fine[b] # t
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![c] = NoTech]
    /\ UNCHANGED << fine, allowance, permits >>

HandBackPermit(t) ==
    /\ t \in permits
    /\ \A c \in Cabinets : coarse[c] # t
    /\ \A b \in Bins : fine[b] # t
    /\ permits' = permits \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, fine, allowance >>

\* Arms come and go, but never below what is already in technicians' hands.
Reprovision(n) ==
    /\ n # allowance
    /\ n >= Cardinality(permits)
    /\ allowance' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, fine, permits >>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Techs : TakePermit(t) \/ HandBackPermit(t)
    \/ \E t \in Techs, c \in Cabinets : TakeCabinet(t, c) \/ ReleaseCabinet(t, c)
    \/ \E t \in Techs, b \in Bins : TakeBin(t, b) \/ ReleaseBin(t, b)
    \/ \E n \in 0..MaxArms : Reprovision(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

FineInterlockCoveredByCoarse ==
    \A b \in Bins : fine[b] # NoTech => coarse[CabinetOf(b)] = fine[b]

====
nl:
A hospital pharmacy runs an automated dispenser. Controlled stock lives in cabinets, and each cabinet is divided into bins. To draw from a bin a technician must first take the cabinet's coarse interlock and then the bin's fine interlock -- the coarse interlock is what keeps two technicians out of the same cabinet, and the fine interlock is what keeps them out of the same bin. Separately, the dispenser only has so many robot arms available, and the pharmacy-in-charge re-provisions that arm allowance at runtime as arms are taken out for cleaning or brought back; a technician needs an arm permit before touching any interlock at all.

A technician without a permit may take one, provided the permits already issued are below the current arm allowance. A technician holding a permit may take the coarse interlock on a cabinet that is not interlocked by anyone. A technician holding the coarse interlock on a cabinet may take the fine interlock on any bin of that cabinet that is not interlocked by anyone. A technician may release a fine interlock it holds. A technician holding a cabinet's coarse interlock may release it, but only once it holds no fine interlock on any bin of that cabinet -- the interlocks must be surrendered fine before coarse. A technician holding no interlock at all may hand its permit back. The pharmacy-in-charge may re-provision the arm allowance to any value that is not below the number of permits currently issued.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A technician holding the fine interlock on a bin always also holds the coarse interlock on that bin's cabinet, so the cabinet interlock covers every bin drawn from it and two technicians are never in the same cabinet.

---- MODULE W4Od17m5p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bags, Replicas, MakeupSlots, NoBag, NoSlot

\* answer[r][s] is the replica's fixed answer for a slot; visible[r] is the
\* subset of its answers that have actually reached the router, in any order.
VARIABLES phase, answer, visible, award

vars == << phase, answer, visible, award >>

Backers(b, s) == {r \in Replicas : answer[r][s] = b}
Seen(b, s) == {r \in Replicas : s \in visible[r] /\ answer[r][s] = b}
Open(b, s) == {r \in Replicas : answer[r][s] = NoBag \/ answer[r][s] = b}
Held(s) == \E c \in Bags : award[c] = s

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in [Bags -> {"queued", "seeking", "awarded", "turned"}]
    /\ answer \in [Replicas -> [MakeupSlots -> Bags \cup {NoBag}]]
    /\ visible \in [Replicas -> SUBSET MakeupSlots]
    /\ award \in [Bags -> MakeupSlots \cup {NoSlot}]

Init ==
    /\ phase = [b \in Bags |-> "queued"]
    /\ answer = [r \in Replicas |-> [s \in MakeupSlots |-> NoBag]]
    /\ visible = [r \in Replicas |-> {}]
    /\ award = [b \in Bags |-> NoSlot]

PutForward(b) ==
    /\ phase[b] = "queued"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "seeking"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << answer, visible, award >>

Name(r, s, b) ==
    /\ answer[r][s] = NoBag
    /\ phase[b] = "seeking"
    /\ answer' = [answer EXCEPT ![r][s] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED << phase, visible, award >>

Surface(r, s) ==
    /\ answer[r][s] # NoBag
    /\ s \notin visible[r]
    /\ visible' = [visible EXCEPT ![r] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << phase, answer, award >>

Award(b, s) ==
    /\ phase[b] = "seeking"
    /\ ~Held(s)
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(Seen(b, s)) > Cardinality(Replicas)
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "awarded"]
    /\ award' = [award EXCEPT ![b] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED << answer, visible >>

\* A bag is only turned away once no slot is still winnable for it.
TurnAway(b) ==
    /\ phase[b] = "seeking"
    /\ \A s \in MakeupSlots :
         \/ Held(s)
         \/ 2 * Cardinality(Open(b, s)) <= Cardinality(Replicas)
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "turned"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << answer, visible, award >>

SendOn(b) ==
    /\ phase[b] = "awarded"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "queued"]
    /\ award' = [award EXCEPT ![b] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED << answer, visible >>

Requeue(b) ==
    /\ phase[b] = "turned"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << answer, visible, award >>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Bags : PutForward(b) \/ TurnAway(b) \/ SendOn(b) \/ Requeue(b)
    \/ \E r \in Replicas, s \in MakeupSlots : Surface(r, s)
    \/ \E r \in Replicas, s \in MakeupSlots, b \in Bags : Name(r, s, b)
    \/ \E b \in Bags, s \in MakeupSlots : Award(b, s)

\* Each bag needs its own fair chance at being named, awarded and turned away;
\* answers are fixed once given, so all of these fire only finitely often.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A b \in Bags :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ SF_vars(\E r \in Replicas, s \in MakeupSlots : Name(r, s, b))
        /\ SF_vars(\E s \in MakeupSlots : Award(b, s))
        /\ SF_vars(TurnAway(b))
    /\ WF_vars(\E r \in Replicas, s \in MakeupSlots : Surface(r, s))

SlotAwardedOnlyToItsMajorityBag ==
    \A b \in Bags :
        award[b] # NoSlot =>
            2 * Cardinality(Backers(b, award[b])) > Cardinality(Replicas)

EverySeekingBagDecided ==
    \A b \in Bags : (phase[b] = "seeking") ~> (phase[b] \in {"awarded", "turned"})

====
nl:
An airport baggage router hands each bag one make-up slot, and it decides which by putting the question to a set of allocator replicas. Each replica will name at most one bag per slot -- once a replica has named a bag for a slot, that is its answer for that slot for the rest of the session. A bag is awarded a slot only when a strict majority of the replicas' answers for that slot, as actually received by the router, name that bag. The replicas' answers travel over the terminal's message fabric, which promises nothing about ordering: answers become visible to the router in any order at all.

A queued bag may be put forward, entering the seeking state. A replica that has not yet answered for a slot may name any seeking bag for that slot. Any answer a replica has given but the router has not yet received may become visible to the router, in whatever order. A seeking bag may be awarded a slot when the answers the router has received for that slot give that bag a strict majority of the replicas and no other bag already holds that slot. A seeking bag is turned away when, for every slot, either the slot is already awarded to another bag or the answers already fixed by the replicas make a majority for this bag impossible. An awarded bag may be sent on its way, releasing its slot back, and a turned-away bag may be re-queued.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A bag that holds a make-up slot is named for that slot by a strict majority of the allocator replicas, so no slot is ever awarded to two different bags.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bag that enters the seeking state is eventually either awarded a slot or turned away.

---- MODULE W4Od9m1p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Substations, Circuits, TotalDemand, MaxSeizures

\* A feeder is owned by exactly one substation; only the token holder may
\* touch its own feeders.
Feeders == Substations \X Circuits
OwnerOf(f) == f[1]

VARIABLES token, carried, pooled, seizures

vars == << token, carried, pooled, seizures >>

RECURSIVE Tally(_)
Tally(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET f == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN carried[f] + Tally(S \ {f})

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Substations
    /\ carried \in [Feeders -> 0..TotalDemand]
    /\ pooled \in 0..TotalDemand
    /\ seizures \in 0..MaxSeizures

Init ==
    /\ token = CHOOSE s \in Substations : TRUE
    /\ carried = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ pooled = TotalDemand
    /\ seizures = 0

PassToken(s) ==
    /\ s # token
    /\ token' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED << carried, pooled, seizures >>

\* Every movement below is a single megawatt leaving one place and arriving
\* in exactly one other.
Transfer(f, g) ==
    /\ OwnerOf(f) = token
    /\ OwnerOf(g) = token
    /\ f # g
    /\ carried[f] > 0
    /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1, ![g] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, pooled, seizures >>

ShedOne(f) ==
    /\ OwnerOf(f) = token
    /\ carried[f] > 0
    /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1]
    /\ pooled' = pooled + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, seizures >>

RestoreOne(f) ==
    /\ OwnerOf(f) = token
    /\ pooled > 0
    /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![f] = @ + 1]
    /\ pooled' = pooled - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, seizures >>

\* The control room's intervention moves the token without the holder.
Seize(s) ==
    /\ s # token
    /\ seizures < MaxSeizures
    /\ token' = s
    /\ seizures' = seizures + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << carried, pooled >>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Substations : PassToken(s) \/ Seize(s)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders, g \in Feeders : Transfer(f, g)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : ShedOne(f) \/ RestoreOne(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DemandIsConserved == Tally(Feeders) + pooled = TotalDemand

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Substations = {subA, subB}
    Circuits = {ckt1, ckt2}
    TotalDemand = 3
    MaxSeizures = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT DemandIsConserved
nl:
A regional grid runs its load-shedding scheme from a ring of substations. Exactly one substation holds the ring token at a time, and only the token holder may move load about. Every megawatt of demand on the system is either being carried by one of the feeders or is parked in the shed pool waiting to be restored; the scheme moves demand between those places but never invents or discards it. Each feeder belongs to one substation. The control room also has a bounded number of privileged interventions it may use during an event.

The token holder may pass the token on to any other substation in the ring. The token holder may transfer one megawatt from one of its own feeders that is carrying load to another of its own feeders. The token holder may shed one megawatt from one of its own feeders into the shed pool. The token holder may restore one megawatt from the shed pool onto one of its own feeders. Finally, the control room may seize the token for any substation directly, spending one of its privileged interventions; this is how the ring is recovered when the holder is unreachable, and it is the only way the token moves without the holder's cooperation.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The demand carried by all the feeders together plus the demand parked in the shed pool always equals the total demand the scheme started with, so load-shedding never creates or destroys demand.

---- MODULE W4Od3m9p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Engines, Instructions, MaxLen, MaxHandovers

\* ackAt[u] is the position the desk promised a member bank for instruction u,
\* or 0 if u has never been acknowledged.
VARIABLES log, ackAt, owner, config, staged

vars == << log, ackAt, owner, config, staged >>

Staged(u) == \E e \in Engines : u \in staged[e]

TypeOK ==
    /\ log \in Seq(Instructions)
    /\ Len(log) <= MaxLen
    /\ ackAt \in [Instructions -> 0..MaxLen]
    /\ owner \in Engines
    /\ config \in 0..MaxHandovers
    /\ staged \in [Engines -> SUBSET Instructions]

Init ==
    /\ log = << >>
    /\ ackAt = [u \in Instructions |-> 0]
    /\ owner = CHOOSE e \in Engines : TRUE
    /\ config = 0
    /\ staged = [e \in Engines |-> {}]

TakeIn(e, u) ==
    /\ e = owner
    /\ ~Staged(u)
    /\ ackAt[u] = 0
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![e] = @ \cup {u}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << log, ackAt, owner, config >>

\* The acknowledgement is the position, so the append and the promise have to
\* agree in the same step.
AppendIn(e, u) ==
    /\ e = owner
    /\ u \in staged[e]
    /\ Len(log) < MaxLen
    /\ log' = Append(log, u)
    /\ ackAt' = [ackAt EXCEPT ![u] = Len(log) + 1]
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![e] = @ \ {u}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, config >>

Discard(e, u) ==
    /\ u \in staged[e]
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![e] = @ \ {u}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << log, ackAt, owner, config >>

\* Handover rotates ownership; whatever an engine had staged stays with it.
Handover ==
    /\ config < MaxHandovers
    /\ config' = config + 1
    /\ owner' = CHOOSE e \in Engines : e # owner
    /\ UNCHANGED << log, ackAt, staged >>

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Engines, u \in Instructions : TakeIn(e, u) \/ AppendIn(e, u) \/ Discard(e, u)
    \/ Handover

\* Discarding is always available to the staging engine, so every staged
\* instruction has a fair way out even when the log is full.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A u \in Instructions :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ SF_vars(\E e \in Engines : AppendIn(e, u) \/ Discard(e, u))

AcknowledgedPositionsStillHold ==
    \A u \in Instructions :
        ackAt[u] # 0 => (ackAt[u] <= Len(log) /\ log[ackAt[u]] = u)

EveryStagedInstructionClears ==
    \A u \in Instructions : Staged(u) ~> ~Staged(u)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Engines = {engLDN, engFRA}
    Instructions = {ins1, ins2, ins3}
    MaxLen = 2
    MaxHandovers = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT AcknowledgedPositionsStillHold

PROPERTY EveryStagedInstructionClears
nl:
Two settlement engines, commissioned years apart by different vendors, share one interbank instruction log. The log is an append-only sequence, and ownership of it rotates: the scheme runs in numbered configurations, and each handover advances the configuration number and moves ownership of the log from the engine that has it to the other one. Only the engine that currently owns the log may take instructions in or append them. When an engine takes an instruction in it is staged, not yet in the log; when it appends the instruction the settlement desk acknowledges the position at which the instruction landed, and that acknowledgement is what a member bank is later shown. The log is only so long: a session's log has a fixed maximum length, and there are more instructions in circulation than places in it.

The owning engine may take in an instruction that is not staged anywhere and has never been acknowledged. The owning engine may append an instruction it has staged, provided the log is not yet at its maximum length: the instruction goes on the end, the desk acknowledges it at that position, and it stops being staged. Either engine may discard an instruction it has staged, which puts it back into circulation unacknowledged. The scheme may hand the log over while it has handovers left in its schedule: the configuration number advances and the other engine becomes the owner, while anything staged stays staged with the engine that took it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every instruction the settlement desk has acknowledged still sits in the shared log at exactly the position it was acknowledged at.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every instruction that is staged by an engine eventually stops being staged, whether by being appended or by being discarded.

---- MODULE W4Od7m7p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Gangs, Free, NoRead, NoGang

\* seen[g] is the value gang g read out of the register; the swap only goes
\* through if the register still agrees with it.
VARIABLES reg, seen, onRail, stalled

vars == << reg, seen, onRail, stalled >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in Gangs \cup {Free}
    /\ seen \in [Gangs -> Gangs \cup {Free, NoRead}]
    /\ onRail \in SUBSET Gangs
    /\ stalled \in Gangs \cup {NoGang}

Init ==
    /\ reg = Free
    /\ seen = [g \in Gangs |-> NoRead]
    /\ onRail = {}
    /\ stalled = NoGang

ReadReg(g) ==
    /\ g # stalled
    /\ seen[g] = NoRead
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![g] = reg]
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, onRail, stalled >>

\* The compare half of compare-and-swap: a gang that stalled across a change
\* of the register cannot claim the rail on the strength of a stale read.
Swap(g) ==
    /\ g # stalled
    /\ seen[g] = Free
    /\ reg = Free
    /\ reg' = g
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![g] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED << onRail, stalled >>

FailedSwap(g) ==
    /\ seen[g] # NoRead
    /\ seen[g] # reg
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![g] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, onRail, stalled >>

Mount(g) ==
    /\ reg = g
    /\ g \notin onRail
    /\ onRail' = onRail \cup {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, seen, stalled >>

Dismount(g) ==
    /\ g \in onRail
    /\ onRail' = onRail \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, seen, stalled >>

\* The register is only handed back once the gang is clear of the rail.
ReleaseReg(g) ==
    /\ reg = g
    /\ g \notin onRail
    /\ reg' = Free
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![g] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED << onRail, stalled >>

Stall(g) == /\ stalled = NoGang /\ stalled' = g /\ UNCHANGED << reg, seen, onRail >>
Resume  == /\ stalled # NoGang /\ stalled' = NoGang /\ UNCHANGED << reg, seen, onRail >>

Next ==
    \/ \E g \in Gangs : ReadReg(g) \/ Swap(g) \/ FailedSwap(g)
    \/ \E g \in Gangs : Mount(g) \/ Dismount(g) \/ ReleaseReg(g) \/ Stall(g)
    \/ Resume

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RailWorkedOnlyByRegisterOwner == \A g \in Gangs : g \in onRail => reg = g

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Gangs = {gngA, gngB, gngC}
    Free = free
    NoRead = noRead
    NoGang = noGang

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT RailWorkedOnlyByRegisterOwner
nl:
A container terminal has one quay crane rail that gangs must have to themselves while they work it. Access is arbitrated by a single compare-and-swap register in the terminal's control system: the register either reads free or names the gang that owns the rail. A gang first reads the register, then swaps its own name in if what it read is still what the register says. Gangs here are slow rather than failed -- at most one gang at a time may stall between its read and its swap, and it always comes back -- which is exactly why the swap has to re-check what the read saw.

A gang that is not stalled and holds no read may read the register, remembering the value it saw. A gang that is not stalled, read the register as free, and finds the register still free may swap its own name in, taking ownership. A gang whose remembered value no longer matches the register discards its read and will read again. A gang named by the register may mount the rail and begin working it. A gang on the rail may dismount. A gang named by the register that is not on the rail may release the register back to free, clearing its read. A gang that is not stalled may stall, and the stalled gang may come back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A gang is never on the quay crane rail unless the compare-and-swap register names that gang, so the rail is worked by at most one gang at a time.
