---- MODULE W4Od14m9p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Drones, Targets, MaxEpoch, MaxWind, ReleaseLimit, NoTarget

\* armed is the tasking system's register of unspent release authorities;
\* struck is the operation's strike record. The invariant ties them together.
VARIABLES epoch, droneEpoch, assignment, armed, struck, wind

vars == << epoch, droneEpoch, assignment, armed, struck, wind >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ droneEpoch \in [Drones -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ assignment \in [Drones -> Targets \cup {NoTarget}]
    /\ armed \in SUBSET Targets
    /\ struck \in SUBSET Targets
    /\ wind \in 0..MaxWind

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ droneEpoch = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ assignment = [d \in Drones |-> NoTarget]
    /\ armed = Targets
    /\ struck = {}
    /\ wind = 0

Assign(d, t) ==
    /\ droneEpoch[d] = epoch
    /\ assignment[d] = NoTarget
    /\ t \in armed
    /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![d] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, droneEpoch, armed, struck, wind >>

\* Spending the authority and recording the strike are the same step, which is
\* what makes the release once-only.
Release(d, t) ==
    /\ assignment[d] = t
    /\ droneEpoch[d] = epoch
    /\ wind <= ReleaseLimit
    /\ t \in armed
    /\ armed' = armed \ {t}
    /\ struck' = struck \cup {t}
    /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![d] = NoTarget]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, droneEpoch, wind >>

\* The commander's override waives the epoch and the wind, but it cannot
\* conjure a release authority that has already been spent.
OverrideRelease(d, t) ==
    /\ assignment[d] = t
    /\ t \in armed
    /\ armed' = armed \ {t}
    /\ struck' = struck \cup {t}
    /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![d] = NoTarget]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, droneEpoch, wind >>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ assignment' = [d \in Drones |-> NoTarget]
    /\ UNCHANGED << droneEpoch, armed, struck, wind >>

Resync(d) ==
    /\ droneEpoch[d] # epoch
    /\ droneEpoch' = [droneEpoch EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, assignment, armed, struck, wind >>

Cancel(d) ==
    /\ assignment[d] # NoTarget
    /\ assignment' = [assignment EXCEPT ![d] = NoTarget]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, droneEpoch, armed, struck, wind >>

Gust(w) ==
    /\ w # wind
    /\ wind' = w
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, droneEpoch, assignment, armed, struck >>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones, t \in Targets : Assign(d, t) \/ Release(d, t) \/ OverrideRelease(d, t)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Resync(d) \/ Cancel(d)
    \/ \E w \in 0..MaxWind : Gust(w)
    \/ Reconfigure

\* Assignment and release both flicker -- with the epoch, with the wind -- so
\* each target needs strong fairness on getting flown and getting hit.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A t \in Targets :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ SF_vars(\E d \in Drones : Assign(d, t))
        /\ SF_vars(\E d \in Drones : Release(d, t) \/ OverrideRelease(d, t))
    /\ \A d \in Drones :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(Resync(d))

ArmedIsExactlyTheUnstruck == armed = Targets \ struck

EveryArmedTargetIsStruck ==
    \A t \in Targets : (t \in armed) ~> (t \in struck)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Drones = {drn1, drn2}
    Targets = {tgt1, tgt2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    MaxWind = 2
    ReleaseLimit = 1
    NoTarget = noTarget

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ArmedIsExactlyTheUnstruck

PROPERTY EveryArmedTargetIsStruck
nl:
A wildfire air operation flies retardant drones. Dropping a load on a target is irreversible: once a target has been treated the load is gone and the operation records the strike. The tasking system therefore keeps an arming register listing the targets that still hold an unspent release authority, and a drone can only release on a target that is still in that register. The swarm's tasking is reconfigured as the fire moves -- each reconfiguration advances the tasking epoch and cancels every drone's current assignment, since assignments made under the old profile no longer describe the fire. Drones carry the epoch they last synchronised to. Wind matters too: a drone will not release above a wind reading over its release limit. The incident commander holds a privileged override for the cases where none of that can be waited out.

A drone synchronised to the current epoch and carrying no assignment may be assigned a target that is still in the arming register. A drone carrying an assignment, synchronised to the current epoch, may release on its target when the wind reading is at or below the release limit and the target is still armed: the target leaves the arming register, the strike is recorded, and the assignment is cleared. The incident commander may order an override release by a drone carrying an assignment whose target is still armed, regardless of that drone's epoch and regardless of the wind. The tasking system may reconfigure while it has profiles left in its schedule, advancing the epoch and cancelling every assignment. A drone whose epoch is behind may resynchronise. A drone may have its assignment cancelled. The wind reading may change to any other value at any time.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The arming register always holds exactly those targets that have not been struck, so no target is ever released on twice.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every target still holding a release authority is eventually struck.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m8p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Techs, Fridges, Racks, NoTech

\* A shelf is addressed coarse-then-fine: refrigerator first, then rack.
Shelves == Fridges \X Racks
FridgeOf(sh) == sh[1]

\* present is who is physically at the bench; stepping away does not hand
\* back custody, it only stops you taking more.
VARIABLES roster, fridgeHeld, shelfHeld, rosteringUp, present

vars == << roster, fridgeHeld, shelfHeld, rosteringUp, present >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ roster \in SUBSET Techs
    /\ fridgeHeld \in [Fridges -> Techs \cup {NoTech}]
    /\ shelfHeld \in [Shelves -> Techs \cup {NoTech}]
    /\ rosteringUp \in BOOLEAN
    /\ present \in SUBSET Techs

Init ==
    /\ roster = {}
    /\ fridgeHeld = [f \in Fridges |-> NoTech]
    /\ shelfHeld = [sh \in Shelves |-> NoTech]
    /\ rosteringUp = TRUE
    /\ present = {}

SignOn(t) ==
    /\ rosteringUp
    /\ t \notin roster
    /\ roster' = roster \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED << fridgeHeld, shelfHeld, rosteringUp, present >>

\* Signing off strips custody in the same movement; leaving it behind is
\* exactly what the safety property forbids.
SignOff(t) ==
    /\ rosteringUp
    /\ t \in roster
    /\ roster' = roster \ {t}
    /\ fridgeHeld' = [f \in Fridges |-> IF fridgeHeld[f] = t THEN NoTech ELSE fridgeHeld[f]]
    /\ shelfHeld' = [sh \in Shelves |-> IF shelfHeld[sh] = t THEN NoTech ELSE shelfHeld[sh]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << rosteringUp, present >>

TakeFridge(t, f) ==
    /\ t \in roster
    /\ t \in present
    /\ fridgeHeld[f] = NoTech
    /\ fridgeHeld' = [fridgeHeld EXCEPT ![f] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED << roster, shelfHeld, rosteringUp, present >>

TakeShelf(t, sh) ==
    /\ t \in present
    /\ fridgeHeld[FridgeOf(sh)] = t
    /\ shelfHeld[sh] = NoTech
    /\ shelfHeld' = [shelfHeld EXCEPT ![sh] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED << roster, fridgeHeld, rosteringUp, present >>

GiveUpShelf(t, sh) ==
    /\ shelfHeld[sh] = t
    /\ shelfHeld' = [shelfHeld EXCEPT ![sh] = NoTech]
    /\ UNCHANGED << roster, fridgeHeld, rosteringUp, present >>

GiveUpFridge(t, f) ==
    /\ fridgeHeld[f] = t
    /\ \A sh \in Shelves : FridgeOf(sh) = f => shelfHeld[sh] # t
    /\ fridgeHeld' = [fridgeHeld EXCEPT ![f] = NoTech]
    /\ UNCHANGED << roster, shelfHeld, rosteringUp, present >>

\* A silent crash: the roster simply stops moving.
CrashRostering ==
    /\ rosteringUp
    /\ rosteringUp' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED << roster, fridgeHeld, shelfHeld, present >>

Arrive(t) == /\ t \notin present /\ present' = present \cup {t} /\ UNCHANGED << roster, fridgeHeld, shelfHeld, rosteringUp >>
StepAway(t) == /\ t \in present /\ present' = present \ {t} /\ UNCHANGED << roster, fridgeHeld, shelfHeld, rosteringUp >>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Techs : SignOn(t) \/ SignOff(t) \/ Arrive(t) \/ StepAway(t)
    \/ \E t \in Techs, f \in Fridges : TakeFridge(t, f) \/ GiveUpFridge(t, f)
    \/ \E t \in Techs, sh \in Shelves : TakeShelf(t, sh) \/ GiveUpShelf(t, sh)
    \/ CrashRostering

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ShelfCustodyIsRostered ==
    \A sh \in Shelves : shelfHeld[sh] # NoTech => shelfHeld[sh] \in roster

====
nl:
A hospital blood bank tracks units of product in refrigerators, each refrigerator divided into shelves. Custody is taken coarse before fine: to work a shelf a technician must first take custody of the refrigerator, and only then of the shelf. Custody is what authorises a technician to touch the inventory record, so a technician who is not on the bank's current duty roster must never be holding any of it. The duty roster is maintained by the hospital's rostering service, and that service can crash silently: it simply stops signing people on and off, with no announcement, so whoever is on the roster at that moment stays on it.

While the rostering service is up, it may sign a technician on to the duty roster. While it is up, it may also sign a technician off, which removes them from the roster and, in the same movement, strips them of every refrigerator and shelf they hold -- signing off never leaves custody behind. A technician may walk up to the bench, and a technician at the bench may step away; stepping away does not hand anything back, it only stops them taking more. A technician on the duty roster who is at the bench may take custody of a refrigerator nobody holds. A technician at the bench holding a refrigerator may take custody of any shelf in it that nobody holds. A technician may give up a shelf it holds. A technician may give up a refrigerator it holds, but only once it holds no shelf inside that refrigerator, so custody is surrendered fine before coarse. The rostering service may crash, after which it neither signs anyone on nor off again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every shelf under custody is held by a technician who is on the blood bank's current duty roster.

---- MODULE W4Od11m5p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Spoolers, Servers, Jobs, MaxGen, NoSpooler

\* An endorsement is only worth anything in the generation it was stamped in.
VARIABLES gen, endorses, endorseGen, job, owner

vars == << gen, endorses, endorseGen, job, owner >>

Backing(sp) == {s \in Servers : endorses[s] = sp /\ endorseGen[s] = gen}
Entitled(sp) == 2 * Cardinality(Backing(sp)) > Cardinality(Servers)

TypeOK ==
    /\ gen \in 0..MaxGen
    /\ endorses \in [Servers -> Spoolers \cup {NoSpooler}]
    /\ endorseGen \in [Servers -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ job \in [Jobs -> {"queued", "onpress", "finished", "rejected"}]
    /\ owner \in [Jobs -> Spoolers \cup {NoSpooler}]

Init ==
    /\ gen = 0
    /\ endorses = [s \in Servers |-> NoSpooler]
    /\ endorseGen = [s \in Servers |-> 0]
    /\ job = [j \in Jobs |-> "queued"]
    /\ owner = [j \in Jobs |-> NoSpooler]

Endorse(s, sp) ==
    /\ endorses[s] = NoSpooler \/ endorseGen[s] # gen
    /\ endorses' = [endorses EXCEPT ![s] = sp]
    /\ endorseGen' = [endorseGen EXCEPT ![s] = gen]
    /\ UNCHANGED << gen, job, owner >>

Start(j, sp) ==
    /\ job[j] = "queued"
    /\ Entitled(sp)
    /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![j] = "onpress"]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![j] = sp]
    /\ UNCHANGED << gen, endorses, endorseGen >>

Finish(j) ==
    /\ job[j] = "onpress"
    /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![j] = "finished"]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![j] = NoSpooler]
    /\ UNCHANGED << gen, endorses, endorseGen >>

Reject(j) ==
    /\ job[j] = "queued"
    /\ \A sp \in Spoolers : ~Entitled(sp)
    /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![j] = "rejected"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << gen, endorses, endorseGen, owner >>

\* Re-sharing the pool voids every endorsement, so nothing may stay on a press
\* across it: the jobs come back to the queue unowned.
ReShare ==
    /\ gen < MaxGen
    /\ gen' = gen + 1
    /\ job' = [j \in Jobs |-> IF job[j] = "onpress" THEN "queued" ELSE job[j]]
    /\ owner' = [j \in Jobs |-> NoSpooler]
    /\ UNCHANGED << endorses, endorseGen >>

Requeue(j) ==
    /\ job[j] \in {"finished", "rejected"}
    /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![j] = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << gen, endorses, endorseGen, owner >>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Servers, sp \in Spoolers : Endorse(s, sp)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs, sp \in Spoolers : Start(j, sp)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Finish(j) \/ Reject(j) \/ Requeue(j)
    \/ ReShare

\* Entitlement flickers as the generation moves, so each job needs strong
\* fairness on its own start and its own finish.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A j \in Jobs :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ SF_vars(\E sp \in Spoolers : Start(j, sp))
        /\ SF_vars(Finish(j))
        /\ SF_vars(Reject(j))
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Servers, sp \in Spoolers : Endorse(s, sp))

PressWorkIsEntitled ==
    \A j \in Jobs : job[j] = "onpress" => Entitled(owner[j])

EveryQueuedJobSettles ==
    \A j \in Jobs : (job[j] = "queued") ~> (job[j] \in {"finished", "rejected"})

====
nl:
A commercial print shop grew by acquisition and now runs two spooler installations that were never meant to coexist: each was sold as the shop's only spooler, and both now drive the same pool of presses. Which spooler is entitled to drive the pool is settled by the print servers: a spooler may only put a job on a press while a strict majority of the servers endorse it for the pool's current sharing generation. Endorsements are stamped with the generation they were given in, and an endorsement from an earlier generation counts for nothing. The generation advances whenever the pool is re-shared between the two installations, and re-sharing pulls every job currently on a press back into the queue, because the spooler that started it may no longer be entitled to the pool.

A print server whose endorsement is missing or stamped with an earlier generation may endorse either spooler for the current generation. A queued job may be started by a spooler that holds a current-generation majority of endorsements, putting the job on a press and recording which spooler owns it. A job on a press may finish. A queued job may be rejected while no spooler holds a current-generation majority. The shop may re-share the pool while it has re-sharings left in its schedule: the generation advances and every job on a press goes back to the queue with no owner. A finished or rejected job may be re-queued for another run.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every job on a press is owned by a spooler that holds endorsements from a strict majority of the print servers stamped with the pool's current sharing generation.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every queued job eventually finishes or is rejected.

---- MODULE W4Od6m6p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Zones, ZoneLimit, LeaseTicks, NoZone, NoCar

\* A lapsed-but-unreclaimed lease still occupies its zone: the dispatcher has
\* not noticed it yet, so it is counted here exactly like a live one.
VARIABLES lease, ttl, demand, outOfContact

vars == << lease, ttl, demand, outOfContact >>

Leased(z) == Cardinality({c \in Cars : lease[c] = z})

TypeOK ==
    /\ lease \in [Cars -> Zones \cup {NoZone}]
    /\ ttl \in [Cars -> 0..LeaseTicks]
    /\ demand \in SUBSET Zones
    /\ outOfContact \in Cars \cup {NoCar}

Init ==
    /\ lease = [c \in Cars |-> NoZone]
    /\ ttl = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ demand = {}
    /\ outOfContact = NoCar

RaiseCall(z) ==
    /\ z \notin demand
    /\ demand' = demand \cup {z}
    /\ UNCHANGED << lease, ttl, outOfContact >>

Grant(c, z) ==
    /\ c # outOfContact
    /\ lease[c] = NoZone
    /\ z \in demand
    /\ Leased(z) < ZoneLimit
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![c] = z]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![c] = LeaseTicks]
    /\ UNCHANGED << demand, outOfContact >>

Renew(c) ==
    /\ c # outOfContact
    /\ lease[c] # NoZone
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![c] = LeaseTicks]
    /\ UNCHANGED << lease, demand, outOfContact >>

\* The dispatcher's clock runs down every live lease together.
Tick ==
    /\ \E c \in Cars : lease[c] # NoZone /\ ttl[c] > 0
    /\ ttl' = [c \in Cars |->
                 IF lease[c] # NoZone /\ ttl[c] > 0 THEN ttl[c] - 1 ELSE ttl[c]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << lease, demand, outOfContact >>

Reclaim(c) ==
    /\ lease[c] # NoZone
    /\ ttl[c] = 0
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![c] = NoZone]
    /\ UNCHANGED << ttl, demand, outOfContact >>

HandBack(c) ==
    /\ lease[c] # NoZone
    /\ demand' = demand \ {lease[c]}
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![c] = NoZone]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![c] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED << outOfContact >>

LoseContact(c) == /\ outOfContact = NoCar /\ outOfContact' = c /\ UNCHANGED << lease, ttl, demand >>
Regain        == /\ outOfContact # NoCar /\ outOfContact' = NoCar /\ UNCHANGED << lease, ttl, demand >>

Next ==
    \/ \E z \in Zones : RaiseCall(z)
    \/ \E c \in Cars, z \in Zones : Grant(c, z)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Renew(c) \/ Reclaim(c) \/ HandBack(c) \/ LoseContact(c)
    \/ Tick \/ Regain

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ZoneLeasesWithinLimit == \A z \in Zones : Leased(z) <= ZoneLimit

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {carA, carB, carC}
    Zones = {lowZone, highZone}
    ZoneLimit = 1
    LeaseTicks = 2
    NoZone = noZone
    NoCar = noCar

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ZoneLeasesWithinLimit
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank divides the building into service zones. A car may only answer calls in a zone it holds a service lease for, and a zone can be leased to only so many cars at once, because the hoistway machinery in a zone cannot take more than that. Leases expire: each lease carries a countdown, and a car must renew before the countdown reaches zero or the lease lapses. A lease that has run down but has not yet been reclaimed still counts against the zone -- the dispatcher has not seen it lapse yet. Cars are slow rather than failed: at most one car at a time is out of contact, and it always comes back.

A hall call may be raised in a zone that has none outstanding. A car in contact that holds no lease may be granted a lease on a zone that has an outstanding hall call, provided the cars already leased into that zone are below the zone's limit; the lease starts with a full countdown. A car in contact holding a lease may renew it, restoring the full countdown. The dispatcher's clock may tick while at least one lease still has countdown left, running down every live lease at once. A car whose lease countdown has reached zero has its lease reclaimed by the dispatcher, which frees its place in the zone. A car holding a lease may hand it back and clear that zone's hall call. Finally, the one car in contact may drop out of contact, and the car out of contact may return.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every service zone, the number of cars holding a lease on that zone never exceeds the zone's lease limit.

---- MODULE W4Od0m0p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Surgeons, TheatreSlots, MaxWrites, NoStamp, NoSurgeon

\* snapStamp/snapCount are the optimistic snapshot; a write only lands if the
\* stamp still matches, which is what keeps the count honest.
VARIABLES stamp, committed, snapStamp, snapCount, away

vars == << stamp, committed, snapStamp, snapCount, away >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ stamp \in 0..MaxWrites
    /\ committed \in 0..TheatreSlots
    /\ snapStamp \in [Surgeons -> (0..MaxWrites) \cup {NoStamp}]
    /\ snapCount \in [Surgeons -> 0..TheatreSlots]
    /\ away \in Surgeons \cup {NoSurgeon}

Init ==
    /\ stamp = 0
    /\ committed = 0
    /\ snapStamp = [s \in Surgeons |-> NoStamp]
    /\ snapCount = [s \in Surgeons |-> 0]
    /\ away = NoSurgeon

ReadPlan(s) ==
    /\ s # away
    /\ snapStamp[s] = NoStamp
    /\ snapStamp' = [snapStamp EXCEPT ![s] = stamp]
    /\ snapCount' = [snapCount EXCEPT ![s] = committed]
    /\ UNCHANGED << stamp, committed, away >>

\* The write-back carries the surgeon's own snapshot count, so a stale stamp
\* would overwrite whatever landed in between.
Book(s) ==
    /\ s # away
    /\ snapStamp[s] = stamp
    /\ snapCount[s] < TheatreSlots
    /\ stamp < MaxWrites
    /\ committed' = snapCount[s] + 1
    /\ stamp' = stamp + 1
    /\ snapStamp' = [snapStamp EXCEPT ![s] = NoStamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED << snapCount, away >>

Retry(s) ==
    /\ snapStamp[s] # NoStamp
    /\ snapStamp[s] # stamp
    /\ snapStamp' = [snapStamp EXCEPT ![s] = NoStamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED << stamp, committed, snapCount, away >>

Abandon(s) ==
    /\ snapStamp[s] # NoStamp
    /\ snapStamp' = [snapStamp EXCEPT ![s] = NoStamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED << stamp, committed, snapCount, away >>

Cancel ==
    /\ committed > 0
    /\ stamp < MaxWrites
    /\ committed' = committed - 1
    /\ stamp' = stamp + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << snapStamp, snapCount, away >>

StepAway(s) == /\ away = NoSurgeon /\ away' = s /\ UNCHANGED << stamp, committed, snapStamp, snapCount >>
ComeBack   == /\ away # NoSurgeon /\ away' = NoSurgeon /\ UNCHANGED << stamp, committed, snapStamp, snapCount >>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Surgeons : ReadPlan(s) \/ Book(s) \/ Retry(s) \/ Abandon(s) \/ StepAway(s)
    \/ Cancel \/ ComeBack

\* Booking and retrying both flicker with the stamp and with who is away, so
\* each surgeon needs strong fairness on closing its own attempt.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A s \in Surgeons :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ SF_vars(Book(s) \/ Retry(s) \/ Abandon(s))

TheatreSlotsNeverOverbooked == committed <= TheatreSlots

EveryAttemptCloses ==
    \A s \in Surgeons : (snapStamp[s] # NoStamp) ~> (snapStamp[s] = NoStamp)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Surgeons = {srgA, srgB}
    TheatreSlots = 2
    MaxWrites = 3
    NoStamp = noStamp
    NoSurgeon = noSurgeon

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT TheatreSlotsNeverOverbooked

PROPERTY EveryAttemptCloses
nl:
A hospital books its operating theatres from a shared day plan. The plan records how many theatre slots have been committed for the day and carries a version stamp. Surgeons do not lock the plan: each reads it, decides, and writes back only if the version stamp is unchanged, retrying if someone got there first. The day has a fixed number of theatre slots and the plan must never commit more than that. Surgeons are slow rather than failed: at most one surgeon at a time is away from the terminal, and they always come back. The plan's version stamp is only good for a fixed number of writes before the day's plan is closed and archived.

A surgeon at the terminal holding no snapshot may read the plan, taking both its version stamp and its committed-slot count. A surgeon at the terminal whose snapshot stamp still matches the plan may commit a booking, provided the count in its own snapshot is below the day's slot count: the plan's committed count becomes that snapshot count plus one, the version stamp advances, and the snapshot is cleared. A surgeon whose snapshot stamp no longer matches the plan retries, discarding the snapshot. A surgeon may abandon its attempt at any time, discarding its snapshot. A booking may be cancelled while any are committed, which lowers the committed count and advances the version stamp. Finally, the one surgeon at the terminal may step away, and the surgeon who stepped away may come back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The day plan's committed slot count never exceeds the number of theatre slots the day actually has.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every surgeon holding a snapshot of the day plan eventually holds none.

---- MODULE W4Od12m0p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Techs, Units, MaxLen, MaxVersion, NoStamp, NoUnit

\* told[t] is what technician t has been told has gone out; it fills in out of
\* order and is deliberately not what the issue check consults.
VARIABLES dlog, version, snap, intent, told

vars == << dlog, version, snap, intent, told >>

InLog(u) == \E i \in 1..Len(dlog) : dlog[i] = u

TypeOK ==
    /\ dlog \in Seq(Units)
    /\ Len(dlog) <= MaxLen
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
    /\ snap \in [Techs -> (0..MaxVersion) \cup {NoStamp}]
    /\ intent \in [Techs -> Units \cup {NoUnit}]
    /\ told \in [Techs -> SUBSET Units]

Init ==
    /\ dlog = << >>
    /\ version = 0
    /\ snap = [t \in Techs |-> NoStamp]
    /\ intent = [t \in Techs |-> NoUnit]
    /\ told = [t \in Techs |-> {}]

ReadLog(t) ==
    /\ snap[t] = NoStamp
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![t] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED << dlog, version, intent, told >>

Pick(t, u) ==
    /\ snap[t] # NoStamp
    /\ intent[t] = NoUnit
    /\ u \notin told[t]
    /\ intent' = [intent EXCEPT ![t] = u]
    /\ UNCHANGED << dlog, version, snap, told >>

\* The unit is checked against the log itself at the moment of issue, because
\* what the technician was told may be both stale and out of order.
Issue(t) ==
    /\ snap[t] = version
    /\ intent[t] # NoUnit
    /\ Len(dlog) < MaxLen
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ ~InLog(intent[t])
    /\ dlog' = Append(dlog, intent[t])
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![t] = NoStamp]
    /\ intent' = [intent EXCEPT ![t] = NoUnit]
    /\ UNCHANGED << told >>

Retry(t) ==
    /\ snap[t] # NoStamp
    /\ snap[t] # version
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![t] = NoStamp]
    /\ intent' = [intent EXCEPT ![t] = NoUnit]
    /\ UNCHANGED << dlog, version, told >>

DropIntent(t) ==
    /\ intent[t] # NoUnit
    /\ intent' = [intent EXCEPT ![t] = NoUnit]
    /\ UNCHANGED << dlog, version, snap, told >>

Confirm(t, u) ==
    /\ InLog(u)
    /\ u \notin told[t]
    /\ told' = [told EXCEPT ![t] = @ \cup {u}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << dlog, version, snap, intent >>

Amend ==
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << dlog, snap, intent, told >>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Techs : ReadLog(t) \/ Issue(t) \/ Retry(t) \/ DropIntent(t)
    \/ \E t \in Techs, u \in Units : Pick(t, u) \/ Confirm(t, u)
    \/ Amend

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoUnitIssuedTwice ==
    \A i \in 1..Len(dlog), j \in 1..Len(dlog) : dlog[i] = dlog[j] => i = j

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Techs = {tchA, tchB}
    Units = {unt1, unt2, unt3}
    MaxLen = 2
    MaxVersion = 3
    NoStamp = noStamp
    NoUnit = noUnit

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoUnitIssuedTwice
nl:
A hospital blood bank issues units of product against a shared dispense log. Issuing a unit is irreversible: once a unit has gone out to a patient it cannot come back, and issuing the same unit twice is the error the bank exists to prevent. Technicians do not lock the log. Each reads it, takes its version stamp, and writes back only if the stamp is unchanged, retrying otherwise. Confirmations of what has been issued reach the technicians' terminals over the hospital's messaging fabric, which makes no ordering promise, so a technician's picture of what has already gone out can be stale and can fill in out of order. The dispense log is only so long: a session's log holds a fixed number of entries, and the bank stocks more units than that.

A technician holding no snapshot may read the log, taking its version stamp. A technician holding a snapshot and no intent may pick a unit it has not yet been told about. A technician holding a snapshot whose stamp still matches the log, and an intent, may issue that unit, provided the log is not yet full and the unit does not already appear in the log -- the check against the log is made at the moment of issue, not against what the technician was told: the unit is appended, the version stamp advances, and the snapshot and intent are cleared. A technician whose stamp no longer matches the log retries, discarding its snapshot and intent. A technician may drop its intent while keeping its snapshot. A confirmation for any unit already in the log may reach any technician, in any order. The bank supervisor may amend the log's record keeping, which advances the version stamp without issuing anything.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No unit ever appears twice in the dispense log, so no unit is issued more than once.

---- MODULE W4Od3m5p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Agents, Banks, Window, NoBank, NoAgent, NoWindow

\* names[a] is the bank agent a is currently naming; the register is only
\* written on a strict majority of ALL agents, since a crash is silent.
VARIABLES names, register, holds, crashed

vars == << names, register, holds, crashed >>

Naming(b) == {a \in Agents : names[a] = b}
Majority(b) == 2 * Cardinality(Naming(b)) > Cardinality(Agents)

TypeOK ==
    /\ names \in [Agents -> Banks \cup {NoBank}]
    /\ register \in Banks \cup {NoBank}
    /\ holds \in [Banks -> {Window, NoWindow}]
    /\ crashed \in Agents \cup {NoAgent}

Init ==
    /\ names = [a \in Agents |-> NoBank]
    /\ register = NoBank
    /\ holds = [b \in Banks |-> NoWindow]
    /\ crashed = NoAgent

Name(a, b) ==
    /\ a # crashed
    /\ names[a] # b
    /\ names' = [names EXCEPT ![a] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED << register, holds, crashed >>

WriteRegister(b) ==
    /\ register = NoBank
    /\ Majority(b)
    /\ register' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED << names, holds, crashed >>

TakeUp(b) ==
    /\ register = b
    /\ holds[b] = NoWindow
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![b] = Window]
    /\ UNCHANGED << names, register, crashed >>

\* The register is only freed by the bank that is actually holding the window.
GiveBack(b) ==
    /\ holds[b] = Window
    /\ register = b
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![b] = NoWindow]
    /\ register' = NoBank
    /\ UNCHANGED << names, crashed >>

Crash(a) ==
    /\ crashed = NoAgent
    /\ crashed' = a
    /\ UNCHANGED << names, register, holds >>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Agents, b \in Banks : Name(a, b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : WriteRegister(b) \/ TakeUp(b) \/ GiveBack(b)
    \/ \E a \in Agents : Crash(a)

\* Nothing can preempt a written register, so weak fairness on each bank's own

nl:
A clearing house allocates the day's scarce settlement window -- the one slot in the netting cycle in which a member bank may settle its position -- and it will not hand that slot to two banks. Which bank gets it is put to the settlement agents: the window's grant register is only written when a strict majority of the agents name the same bank. One agent may crash silently: it stops naming anyone, and nobody is told, which is why the majority is taken over all the agents and not just the ones still answering. A bank that has been granted the window takes it up before it settles, and the register is only freed when the bank that holds it gives it back.

An agent that has not crashed may name any member bank, replacing whatever name it was carrying. When the grant register is free and a strict majority of the agents name the same bank, the register may be written with that bank. A bank named by the grant register that is not already holding the window may take it up. A bank holding the window may give it back, which frees the register for the next allocation. One agent may crash, after which it never names anyone again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A bank only ever holds the settlement window while the grant register names that bank, so the window is never held by two banks at once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the grant register names a bank, that bank eventually holds the settlement window.

CONSTANTS Servers, Enrolments, MaxOverrides

\* Striking a certified enrolment from every ballot is what makes the
\* certification once-only: the quorum cannot re-form behind it.
VARIABLES docket, ballot, certified, overrides, maintenance

vars == << docket, ballot, certified, overrides, maintenance >>

Voters(e) == {s \in Servers : e \in ballot[s]}
Carried(e) == 2 * Cardinality(Voters(e)) > Cardinality(Servers)
Strike(e) == [s \in Servers |-> ballot[s] \ {e}]

TypeOK ==
    /\ docket \in SUBSET Enrolments
    /\ ballot \in [Servers -> SUBSET Enrolments]
    /\ certified \in SUBSET Enrolments
    /\ overrides \in 0..MaxOverrides
    /\ maintenance \in SUBSET Servers

Init ==
    /\ docket = {}
    /\ ballot = [s \in Servers |-> {}]
    /\ certified = {}
    /\ overrides = 0
    /\ maintenance = {}

PutForward(e) ==
    /\ e \notin certified
    /\ e \notin docket
    /\ docket' = docket \cup {e}
    /\ UNCHANGED << ballot, certified, overrides, maintenance >>

Vote(s, e) ==
    /\ s \notin maintenance
    /\ e \in docket
    /\ e \notin certified
    /\ e \notin ballot[s]
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![s] = @ \cup {e}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << docket, certified, overrides, maintenance >>

Certify(e) ==
    /\ e \in docket
    /\ e \notin certified
    /\ Carried(e)
    /\ certified' = certified \cup {e}
    /\ ballot' = Strike(e)
    /\ docket' = docket \ {e}
    /\ UNCHANGED << overrides, maintenance >>

\* The registrar's direct certification skips the vote but not the striking.
RegistrarCertify(e) ==
    /\ e \notin certified
    /\ overrides < MaxOverrides
    /\ certified' = certified \cup {e}
    /\ ballot' = Strike(e)
    /\ docket' = docket \ {e}
    /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << maintenance >>

Withdraw(e) ==
    /\ e \in docket
    /\ docket' = docket \ {e}
    /\ ballot' = Strike(e)
    /\ UNCHANGED << certified, overrides, maintenance >>

GoDown(s) == /\ s \notin maintenance /\ maintenance' = maintenance \cup {s} /\ UNCHANGED << docket, ballot, certified, overrides >>
ComeUp(s) == /\ s \in maintenance /\ maintenance' = maintenance \ {s} /\ UNCHANGED << docket, ballot, certified, overrides >>

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Enrolments : PutForward(e) \/ Certify(e) \/ RegistrarCertify(e) \/ Withdraw(e)
    \/ \E s \in Servers, e \in Enrolments : Vote(s, e)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : GoDown(s) \/ ComeUp(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CertifiedLeavesNoBallotStanding ==
    \A e \in Enrolments : e \in certified => \A s \in Servers : e \notin ballot[s]

nl:
A university certifies completed enrolments. Certifying an enrolment is irreversible: the certificate goes onto the student's permanent transcript and the university has no mechanism to take it back, so an enrolment must never be certified twice. Certification is decided by the registry's servers: an enrolment is certified when a strict majority of the servers have voted for it. When an enrolment is certified, its entry is struck from every server's ballot in the same movement, so the majority that certified it cannot be standing a second time. Servers go in and out of maintenance and will not vote while they are down. The registrar's office also holds a bounded number of privileged certifications it may issue directly.

An enrolment that has not been certified and is not already before the registry may be put forward. A server that is not in maintenance may vote for an enrolment that is before the registry and not yet certified, if it has not already voted for it. An enrolment before the registry that a strict majority of the servers have voted for may be certified: it joins the permanent transcript, it is struck from every server's ballot, and it leaves the registry's docket. The registrar may certify an uncertified enrolment directly, spending one privileged certification, which likewise strikes it from every ballot and from the docket. An enrolment before the registry may be withdrawn, which also strikes it from every ballot. A server may go into maintenance, and a server in maintenance may come back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No certified enrolment is left standing on any server's ballot, so the majority that certified it can never form again for a second certification.
